command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET faithfully repeats the source but an action target is not proved GETtable; readable JSON or an error cannot validate reset metadata, and replacing it with POST without a scope decision would be unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: GET the validated Manager resource and advertised Actions/ActionInfo metadata only; if reset execution is explicitly selected, POST one documented ResetType after OK and perform bounded recovery validation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The named Manager.Reset target and 15/10 timing are preserved, but no ManagerId, method, ResetType, payload or outage interval is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate read-only action discovery from disruptive invocation and make the selected branch explicit in evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Rejects unsupported action-target GET and adds method/payload discovery, approval, outage and recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Inspection proves only the advertised action contract; execution adds actual BMC reset and return-to-service coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Manager reset may terminate the reviewing connection, interrupt monitoring and leave state unknown after timeout. Host power state should not be assumed unaffected without firmware documentation.

No log clearing or unrelated mutation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item and GET procedure consistently attempt to read Manager.Reset. Their action semantics are underdefined, but there is no competing Master instruction requiring POST.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Vendor action metadata plus an engineer scope choice can define a safe inspection or approved reset path. These are identifiable prerequisites, so REQUIRES applies rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Corrects the false no-risk action-target read and introduces a strict branch between metadata inspection and explicitly authorized reset execution.
independent_technical_reasoning: An action URI identifies an invocation endpoint, not necessarily a readable resource; even a friendly JSON error does not establish supported ResetTypes. Conversely, turning the GET into POST changes a read-only case into an outage-producing BMC reset. The safe resolution is to discover the action from the Manager resource, record its contract, and force an explicit scope decision. If execution is selected, lost connectivity makes retry ambiguous, so one-shot invocation and independent recovery observation are essential.
